response.sql: SELECT SUM(g - l) AS total_g_minus_l, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM manager_half WHERE w >= 26;

assumptions.assumption: Records with a NULL in g or l drop out of the SUM, since SQL arithmetic with NULL yields NULL and SUM skips it. The count is COUNT(*) over all records with w >= 26, so records with NULL g or l are still counted. Records with NULL w are excluded by the w >= 26 filter.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the records that contribute a value to the total, i.e. those with w >= 26 and both g and l present.
